declared_convention_sources.claim_used: Bulk copper has a face-centered-cubic crystal structure.

declared_convention_sources.title: U.S. Department of Energy — Fundamentals Handbook, Material Science, Volume 1
declared_convention_sources.claim_used: Used for crystalline periodic order, grain and boundary definitions, real-crystal imperfections, iron BCC/FCC polymorphism, valence-electron dependence, and metallic versus ionic bonding.

verdict_audit.audit: Copper is explicitly identified as FCC crystalline material.
A crystalline lattice is a periodically repeating three-dimensional array; the statement incorrectly extends that long-range lattice to liquid.
Iron changes between BCC ferrite and FCC austenite with temperature.
A grain is a continuous crystal region with an orientation, but real crystals contain point, line and interfacial imperfections; therefore 'perfect order' is too strong.
The electronic and valence structure controls chemical electron transfer and therefore oxidation tendency; actual oxidation rate also depends on temperature, environment, transport and surface state.

Metallic iron is held by metallic bonding with mobile delocalized electrons; an ionic bond requires attraction between oppositely charged species and is not a bond between identical positive iron ion cores.
